chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: 'Muhammad ibn Abi Umair narrated to us from Zayd al-Narsy, who said: I heard Ubayd ibn Zurara asking Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)'

about the fasting of the day of Ashura, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever fasts it, his share from the fasting of that day is the share of Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad.' I said, 'And what is their share from that day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Fire. May Allah protect us from the Fire and from the deed which brings one closer to the Fire.'

key_terms.ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ: Ibn Marjana (a historical figure associated with the Umayyads, often cited in this context)
key_terms.يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ: The day of Ashura (10th of Muharram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and significance of fasting on the day of Ashura according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of fasting on the 10th of Muharram by comparing the reward to that of Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad, key figures in the Umayyad era known for their role in the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (AS). This comparison suggests that while the fast is accepted and serves as a means of deliverance from the Fire, it does not carry the same high merit as fasting on other significant days, reflecting the Shia view of Ashura as a day of mourning rather than one of great celebratory reward. The Imam’s concluding supplication emphasizes seeking refuge from the Fire, aligning the fast with the broader theme of salvation from divine punishment.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Isa who said, ‘Muhammad in Abu Umeyr narrated to us, from Zayd Al Narsy who said, ‘I heard Zurara asking Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting of the day of Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram).

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who Fasts it, his share from the Fast of that day would be a share of Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad’. I said, ‘And what is their share from that day?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fire. We<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the Fire and from the deed which takes one closer to the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa who has said that narrated to us Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Zayd al-Narsiy who has said the following: “I heard Zurarah asking abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the fast on the day of ‘Ashura’.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Whoever fasts that day, his share for such fast is like the share of ibn Marjanah and the family of Ziyad.’ I then asked, ‘What was their share of that day ? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the fire, I seek protection with Allah against it and against the deeds that take one closer to the fire.’”
